# OpenAI updates ChatGPT for complex questions, web search and images
 Dataist 
OpenAI has updated ChatGPT to answer complex everyday questions more reliably, search the web and work with images

OpenAI has begun rolling out GPT-6.2 Sol, a version of ChatGPT tuned for conversations. It is available worldwide to Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users. The company says the model handles complex requests and web searches better than GPT-6, and asks more relevant follow-up questions. In internal tests, GPT-6.2 interpreted images more accurately — 71.7% versus 47.4% — and followed complex instructions more often: 78.1% versus 62.5%.

## OpenAI releases GPT-6.2 Sol for complex requests and web search

## Test results

On an internal benchmark of expert-level tasks, GPT-6.2 outperformed GPT-6 at all four reasoning levels: Instant, Medium, High and Extra high. The new model scored roughly 65% to just over 71%, while GPT-6 scored about 52–66%.

OpenAI also uses an internal version of BrowseComp to test how models find answers to difficult questions on the web. GPT-6.2 led at every level and, at the highest level, outperformed GPT-6 by about 10 percentage points.

## Safety and access

According to the system card, GPT-6.2 follows safety rules in 91–94% of difficult conversations. GPT-6 scored 77–80%. The most notable progress was in teen safety, covering emotional dependence, eating disorders and dangerous activities.

The results apply only to ChatGPT’s chat mode. The Work and Codex models have not changed. Enterprise administrators can decide whether their users get access to GPT-6.2.

Dataist’s take: GPT-6.2 improves several aspects of ChatGPT at once, but the results cited come from OpenAI’s internal tests. The update also does not extend to Work and Codex, and Enterprise access depends on administrators’ decisions.

# Google正式推出Gemini 4 Neon模型

谷歌开发者 2026-11-24 13

### 描述

作者：

Koray Kavukcuoglu, Google DeepMind 高级副总裁兼 Google 首席 AI 架构师

今天，我们正式推出 Gemini 4 Neon，将前沿级智能带入复杂的软件工程、知识工作及科学研究工作流，快速实现端到端任务。

在超高 (xhigh) 思考模式下，Neon 在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数上取得了 61 分的成绩，超越了同级别模型并位列总榜第三，仅次于体量更大、速度更慢的模型。Neon 在 Vals Index 中排名第二，并跻身帕累托前沿 (Pareto frontier)。除了不断突破模型的基础能力上限，我们也在持续优化模型的使用体验 —— 在全新的 Agent Arena 指数中，Neon 的可操控性 (即在任务中精准适应用户纠正指令的能力) 排名第二。同时，Neon 还擅长遵循多步骤指令，并延续了我们在抑制信息虚构方面的进展，在 Google Antigravity 的内部测试中创下了迄今为止最低的幻觉率。

该模型定价为每百万输入 token 3 美元 (缓存输入 token 享 0.5 折优惠，仅需 0.15 美元/百万)，每百万输出 token 15 美元，并支持 100 万 token 的上下文窗口。

即日起，Gemini 4 Neon 正式登陆以下平台：Google AI Studio 中的 Gemini API、Gemini 企业 (支持 API 调用及模型下拉菜单选择)，以及面向 Google AI Pro 与 Ultra 付费订阅用户的 Google Antigravity 和 Gemini App。

全面赋能企业级办公

深度分析与科研工作

企业日常业务高度依赖电子表格、PDF 文档、图表及音视频资料。Neon 能够在单个 100 万 token 上下文窗口内同步处理各类异构数据，并将其整合为结构化交付物。在多项独立评测中，Neon 均跻身行业第一梯队：在 Vals Index 中排名第二 (70.9%)，并在 Legal Research Bench 与 Tax Agent Bench 两个榜单中排名第一。

在 Surge AI 的多维度测试中，Neon 同样表现优异，包揽了金融、财会、电子表格建模及复杂约束遵循等多项基准测试的榜首；在专攻高密度专业图表解读的 Chartography 评测中拿下 73.5%；在 Agents' Last Exam v1.1 (75.8%) 上与顶尖模型表现不相上下；更在 Zapier 的 AutomationBench (56.3%) 以及模拟长期商业运营的 Andon Labs Vending-Bench 2 (16,843 美元) 中均位列总榜第一。此外，在涵盖 4,200 余个真实智能体会话的 Arena 全新 Agent Arena Index 中，Neon 首秀即以 1,336 分位居全球第二。

而在涵盖量化分析、数学及前沿科研难题的科学与数学推理领域，Neon 在 Terminal-Bench Science (70.5%)、RiemannBench (84.0%) 与 HLE-Diamond (71.3%) 上均刷新了同类最佳成绩。

Methodology: deepmind.google/models/evals-methodology/gemini-4-neon

"Gemini 4 Neon 善于将零散信息梳理为清晰、有据可依的洞察，在日常职场任务中实现了质量、成本与速度的绝佳平衡。在我们的早期评估中，它的整体性能持平甚至超越了 Gemini 4 Carbon，但速度达到其 3 倍，成本却仅为 60%。我们非常期待将这项能力带给 Glean 客户，助力他们处理对精度、细节和时效都有严苛要求的多步骤任务。"—— Thai Tran，Glean AI 产品负责人

"在我们的评测中，Gemini 4 Neon 位列 Medical Index 及内部生命科学基准测试榜首，同时保持了极高的性价比与响应速度。"—— Brandon Valafar，Micro1 战略 AI 负责人

"Neon 比我们以往测试过的任何 Gemini 模型都更加严谨、细致。它能迅速了解大型代码库的脉络与复杂架构；在网络安全评估中，Neon 仅消耗极少量的 token 便找出了其他模型遗漏的多个隐蔽漏洞。对于追求高性价比的代码探索与研究任务，它是不可多得的工具。"—— Karina Nguyen，Thoughtful Lab 创始人

"初级研究员通常按部就班地执行既定实验，而卓越的研究员则会不断追问 '为什么'。Gemini 4 Neon 是首个带给我这种体验的模型。它会持续探索 —— 主动搜寻新数据、发掘可提取的新信号，以训练出更优秀的模型。它也是我们见过的首个无需人工监督就能不断自我完善的模型：面对不理想的实验结果，Neon 不会轻言放弃，而是主动重新设计建模策略，直至取得更优突破。"—— Trenton Chang，Quadrillion 首席科学家

"Gemini 4 Neon 在机器学习工程、数据工程、实验管理及架构设计方面都是极为可靠的得力助手。它善于听取反馈、做事严谨、主动验证假设，且深谙既有技术脉络，让整个 AI 模型研发流程变得前所未有的顺畅。"—— Andrew Carr，Cartwheel 联合创始人兼首席科学家

专为构建生产级代码而打造

Neon 专为长周期智能体工作流而设计，能够在复杂且重度依赖工具的端到端任务中保持稳定表现 —— 无论是独立运行，还是在 Google Antigravity 中担任高速、高判断能力的编排器，统筹调度并行的 Hydrogen 子智能体，均能游刃有余。它不仅大幅减少了冗余的文件读取操作、在执行过程中实时同步进度，还能在长会话中可靠地完成上下文压缩。

在核心开发者与研究人员工作流中，Neon 展现出前沿水准的性能，在同级别前沿模型中极具竞争力。它在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数上以 58.6 分位列总榜第一，并在 Terminal-Bench 4.1 中斩获 65.2% 的分数，在 FrontierCode 2.0 (默认高思考模式下) 取得 46.2% 的成绩。面向生产级代码场景，Neon 能够通过精准的 "外科手术式" 修改，实现跨代码库的多文件调试与重构。在 SWE-sweep 基准测试中，它不仅在 mini-SWE 评估框架下领先 (12.8%)，在 Google Antigravity 中更是超过三倍的达到业界领先的 39.0%，充分释放了 Antigravity 运行框架的性能。

通过在 Google Antigravity 中驱动 Blender MCP，Gemini 4 Neon 借助 /swarm 功能构建了一个照片级逼真的 3D 实验室工作台，以精准的化学元素特征将模型名称视觉化：将本生灯火焰与 Gemini 4 Carbon 及 Gemini 4 Hydrogen 相匹配，将高压气体放电管与 Gemini 4 Argon 及 Neon 相匹配。

在 Google Antigravity 中，Gemini 4 Neon 基于真实的勃朗峰与霞慕尼高程地形，从零编写了一款第一人称 WebGL2 自由式滑雪模拟器 —— 集成了 10,200 行自定义着色器代码、覆盖六条高山雪道的 120 Hz 滑雪物理引擎、动态雪板刻滑轨迹、板状雪崩模拟以及空间 Web Audio 音效，且未使用任何预制素材。

在 Google Antigravity 中借助 /swarm 功能，Gemini 4 Neon 调取历史档案照片，以交互式 3D 形式复原了艾伦·图灵 1936 年在剑桥大学国王学院的书房 —— 从室外的国王学院礼拜堂到室内的 X.8 房间悉数呈现，书桌上甚至还摆放着一台可实际运行的通用图灵机。

在 Google Antigravity 中，由 Gemini 4 Neon 驱动的智能体集群在不使用任何嵌入式图片和 Apps Script 脚本的前提下，仅凭一张图片便构建出了一个包含 10 万个单元格的 Google 表格 —— 利用超过 50 万个实时电子表格公式实现边缘检测、3D 深度映射，并支持在六种交互模式下对场景进行重新打光。

为生产级工作流

带来更高效率与可控性

随着每一次新模型迭代，我们都在不断精进 "思考层级" 设计，为团队提供更细腻的控制粒度与更平滑的档位过渡。Neon 的四个思考层级呈稳步递进，让团队可以根据每项业务负载的实际需求，灵活调节智能水平与 token 消耗。

在多项第三方基准测试中，Neon 均以更低的单任务成本实现了卓越性能。在默认的高 (high) 思考层级下，它不仅在 Artificial Analysis 智能指数上拿下了高分，单任务成本还比 Carbon 降低了 32%；同样在高思考层级下，它在 Vals Index 与 Agent Arena 中双双跻身帕累托前沿，单任务成本较顶尖竞争模型低约 50% 至 80%。针对最严苛的工程、分析与科研任务，超高 (xhigh) 思考层级可展开更深度的多步推理。Neon 释放出其最高智能水准，而单任务成本仍比竞争模型在最高配置下低 36% 以上。

打造高效、前沿级的网络防御能力

随着智能体编程的普及，从代码编写之初就筑牢安全防线至关重要。Gemini 4 Neon for cyber 在 AutoBaxBench 的简单、中等及困难全部等级测试中，生成的安全代码质量均超越了 Carbon，并在高难度层级取得了业界领先成绩 (76%)。

系统防御更在于先于攻击者一步主动排查隐患。渗透测试一直是企业网络安全的基石：在 WebExploitBench v1.2 上，Neon 取得了业界领先的成绩 (51.26%)，而成本仅为同类大模型的一半。

为了全面加固现有代码资产，Neon for cyber 在代码安全强化的全生命周期 —— 漏洞挖掘、漏洞验证与漏洞修复 —— 均展现出前沿水准，同时在运行速度与成本控制上全面领先于大型前沿模型：

精准挖掘代码漏洞：Neon 在 SEC-bench Pro 上取得业界领先表现 (90.5%)，单次测试成本仅为同类的一半左右。

通过漏洞利用验证风险：为了合理排定修复优先级，安全团队需要模型判断漏洞是否具备可利用性。在 ExploitGym 评测中，Neon 仅消耗 Carbon 一半的 token 便达到了前沿级验证水准。

从根源修复漏洞：彻底修补漏洞根源是网络防御闭环的关键一步。Neon 在 Collinear 的 CWE-bench v2 上达到 70.7%，较 Carbon 提升了 3.4 个百分点。

专为安全、可靠执行而设计

Gemini 4 Neon 继承并升级了 Gemini 4 安全防护技术栈 —— 在严防严重滥用与提示词注入方面保持了与 Gemini 4 Carbon 同等严密的防线，同时在模型对齐与智能体行为规范上更进一步。针对承担高强度、长周期生产任务的模型，我们重点打磨了以下三大防线：

降低前沿滥用安全风险：由于 Neon 将前沿级能力下放到了速度更快、成本更低的模型中，我们为其配备了与 Carbon 保护机制相当的实安全防护，以防犯网络与生物安全的滥用，同时大幅减少了对此类领域合法工作的 "误伤"，例如在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上的任务拒绝率仅为 1.98%，在 Terminal-Bench-Science 上更是实现了 0% 误拒。

推进对齐与规范的模型行为：在内部编码使用中，我们的思维链与行为偏离监测器触发的警报率始终低于 Carbon 设定的本已极低的基线水平，这表明 Neon 具有更出色的对齐倾向 —— 且该监测器也已部署至外部应用场景，为 Neon 提供防护。Neon 经过训练，能够在不偷工减料、不捏造结果且不越过用户边界的前提下完成多步骤工作，持续优化 "彻底执行请求" 与 "严守范围" 之间的平衡。它在 Terminal-Bench 4.0 上与 Carbon 同样实现了 0.0% 的作弊率，并在我们的编码作弊评估中仅在 2.45% 的任务上 "走捷径"(为所有 Gemini 4 模型中最低)。此外，它在我们的智能体安全测试套件中实现了 0.09% 的偏离行为率，并在智能体诚实度评估中取得了 99.2% 的通过率。

在我们的智能体行为评估中，Neon 在 Carbon 稳健基线的基础上进一步优化，在不同思考强度设置下，将服务不足 (under-service) 比例降低了 43%–56%，并将越权行为 (overreach) 比例降低了 15%–35%。

抵御间接提示词注入攻击：在 Gray Swan 的 IPI 基准测试中，当网页、邮件、文档或代码中暗藏恶意指令时，Neon 展现出超越同类模型的抗攻击韧性。测试显示，在开启实时防护且处于最高思考层级时，Neon 成功抵御了 Gray Swan 基准测试中的全部攻击，实现了仅少数 Gemini 模型才能达到的 0.0% 攻击成功率。

如需了解完整技术细节，请参阅 Gemini 4 Neon 模型卡片。

专为深度分析而生

在 Gemini 应用中，Gemini 4 Neon 擅长处理既需要前沿级推理能力，又要求迅捷响应的任务。

更高质量的写作与知识工作：Neon 行文清晰，回复结构严谨，且语气自然直白。它能够更精准地读取上传的电子表格、PDF 和图片，将繁杂冗长的资料转化为实用的报告与摘要，并在需要时自动从Gmail 和Google文档中提取相关细节。

可靠的研究与分析：Neon 能够频繁整合来自全网各种信源的细节，针对快速变化的话题提供最新回复，例如在重大采购前对比各家供应商的价格，或是结合最新市场数据整理复杂的简报。

为高难度任务提供快速助力：借助Gemini Neon 中的任务 (Tasks) 功能，相比大型模型，它能以更快的速度、更高的效率完成复杂的多步骤任务。 当您将繁琐的待办事项交给它处理时，例如分析账单明细以找出水电煤费用激增的原因，或交叉核对多张收据和单据以协商退款，它不仅能完成更多工作，还能进一步延长使用额度。

Neon 在 Gemini 4 系列中的定位

Neon 专为复杂编码、分析推理以及生产级企业工作流而打造。Carbon 负责攻克最艰巨的长周期项目，Hydrogen 负责处理快速的日常执行，而 Neon 则在深度与效率之间取得平衡。在复杂且高频的工作流中，Neon 能够更快、更具成本效益地提供前沿级的推理能力。

# Gemini 4 智能体设计量子算法：Lean 证明兜底，arcsin 例程成本降 290 倍

11 月 23 日，Google DeepMind 和 Google Quantum AI 发了一篇博客：一群 Gemini 4 智能体分成几个团队，各自去改进已有的量子算法，每个新程序都必须在 Lean 定理证明器里证明「结果对」和「成本是多少」，才算数。改进最大的一项是一个 arcsin 算术例程，估算成本降到原来的 1/290。

这件事值得拆开看，原因不在 290 这个数字。量子算法有个老难题：大规模电路现在既没法在经典计算机上模拟，也没法在现有的小量子芯片上跑，写出来对不对，只能靠人推导。DeepMind 的做法是把「验证」交给 Lean，再让智能体放开去搜。这套「AI 搜索 + 形式化证明兜底」的组合，前几周已经在数学（三元哥德巴赫、黎曼猜想的 Lean 证明）和软件（AlphaProof Code 验证 Signal 协议）上出现过，这次轮到了量子计算。

## 它是什么

项目 | 内容 
---|---
发布 | 2026-11-23 DeepMind 博客；论文 arXiv 2611.09822（v1 11-06，当前 v3 11-16），25 位作者 
参与方 | Google DeepMind、Google Quantum AI 
用的模型 | 论文称大规模实验都用 Gemini 4 Carbon 
任务 | 5 个：并行 Grover 搜索、定点 arcsin、聚变相关的阻止本领计算、光化学分子动力学、药物代谢酶 P450 
开放内容 | Lean 库 google-deepmind/formal-quantum-computation（Apache 2.0）、问题规范、已验证的解（在 discoveries 分支） 
没开放 | 协调智能体团队的系统、提示词 
能不能在真机上跑 | 不能。所有改进都是资源估算，官方承认仍超出第一代纠错量子计算机的能力 

## 为什么非得用 Lean

先说清楚「成本」指什么。论文用的是容错量子计算里常见的时空成本 Q·𝒯：逻辑量子比特数乘以 T 门数。T 门在纠错码上最贵，所以这个乘积大致对应一台容错机器要算多久、要多大。

问题在于，这些电路动辄几千个逻辑比特、10¹⁴ 量级的成本，经典计算机模拟不了。以前用 AI 搜算法（比如 AlphaEvolve 一类），靠的是「跑一下看分数」，可量子电路跑不了，只能在小规模、能模拟的门集里搜。论文图 1 把这个画得很直白：只靠数值测试，AI 只能找到经典可模拟的解；arcsin 任务里，这就意味着被锁在一个受限门集里。

Lean 换掉的就是「跑一下」这一步。证明不依赖规模，几千比特的电路也能证。

## 原理：规范、验证器、工作流

论文说他们只固定三样东西，团队内部怎么分工不做规定（原文：we prescribe no internal team design）。
研究者写规范（Lean 文件，程序和证明留空 sorry）
        │
        ▼
 ┌─ 团队 1 ─┐ ┌─ 团队 2 ─┐ … ┌─ 团队 N ─┐   各自写程序、补证明
 └────┬────┘ └────┬────┘   └────┬────┘   Lean 内核报错就改
      │ 提交       │            │
      ▼            ▼            ▼
   外部验证器：Lean Comparator 对照冻结的规范
   （定理、定义、允许的公理有没有被改）
      │ 通过
      ▼
   共享 wiki：每题当前最优解、可复用引理、好思路、死胡同
      ▲
      │ 每 4 小时一次「会议」：批评提案、讨论未验证的猜想

### 规范：带资源计数的量子 Hoare 逻辑

Lean 里原本有 Mathlib 和 Physlib 的量子信息库，但缺两样东西，作者自己补上了：

- 一门经典-量子混合的编程语言。经典部分有赋值、条件分支、无界循环；量子部分有酉变换、程序中途测量、比特重置。
- 配套的经典-量子 Hoare 逻辑，并带资源计数。

正确性写成「前置条件、程序、后置条件」三元组，证明时从后置条件往回算最弱前置条件。成本可以证期望值上界，也可以证最坏情况上界，跨分支、跨循环都行。

每个任务就是一个 Lean 文件，里面写好目标定理（「这个程序算对了」和「这个程序的成本不超过 X」），候选程序和证明留成sorry，等智能体来填。

### 验证器：防的是智能体作弊

论文直说智能体会钻规范的空子：弱化定理、改定义、偷加公理。所以每个提交都要过一个外部检查，用 Lean Comparator 对照冻结的规范，确认目标定理、定义和公理白名单都没动过。

这个设计带来一个好处：研究者不用审几千行程序和证明，只要审规范本身。反过来说，结果可不可信，全看规范写没写对。后面讲局限时会再回到这一点。

### 工作流：wiki 加定期会议

博客和论文都强调了多团队协作：

- wiki：只收经过验证的东西。新团队可以直接从 wiki 上的最优解起步，死胡同也记下来，免得别人重走。
- 会议：每 4 小时一次，各团队派智能体参加。这里可以讨论还没证出来的猜想，但猜想要验证通过才算结果。

论文给了一个消融：在三个科学模拟任务上，从两个共享渠道都打开以后算起，把成本下降按对数拆分，61% 来自团队内部，15% 来自跨团队 wiki，24% 来自会议。也就是说，大约四成改进是在团队之间传出来的。各任务差别很大：

任务 | 这段时间总改进 | 团队内 | wiki | 会议 
---|---|---|---|---
阻止本领（聚变） | 7.0× | 87% | 9% | 约 4% 
非 BO 动力学（光化学） | 3.1× | 59% | 12% | 29% 
P450（药物代谢） | 2.5× | 37% | 25% | 38% 
三项合计 | — | 61% | 15% | 24% 

论文图 5 还追了一个思路的传播：聚变任务里，团队 2 先提出一个 288 比特的辅助寄存器方案，团队 3 把它收窄到 231 比特，最后的版本是 210 比特。这很像人类研究组之间的接力。

## 结果和背后的技巧

以下数字都是论文自报（官方称），基线是作者整理过的已发表方案：

任务 | 基线 Q·𝒯 | 本文 | 改进 
---|---|---|---
25 位定点 arcsin（误差 ≤ 1.25×10⁻⁷） | > 1.08×10⁸ | 3.70×10⁵（100 个比特，3,698 个 T 门） | > 290× 
聚变：α 粒子在温稠密氢中的阻止本领 | 5.42×10¹⁵ | 4.59×10¹⁴ | 11.8× 
光化学：C₂₃H₂₀N₃O 非 Born–Oppenheimer 动力学 | 4.98×10¹⁵ | 6.06×10¹⁴ | 8.22× 
药物代谢：细胞色素 P450 | 1.09×10¹² | 4.37×10¹¹ | 2.49× 
并行 Grover 搜索 | 最强已发表协议 | 找任一目标最多 1.22×，找全部 k 个最多 2.57× | — 

逻辑比特数也降了：聚变从 5,650 降到 4,338，P450 从 481 降到 333（博客数据）。

几个改进的来路，论文写得比较具体：

- arcsin：先在一个能经典模拟的门集（kickmix）里搜，成本降到 4.15×10⁵；再靠 Lean 解除门集限制，系数查找环节的门数少了 33%，总成本再降 11%。第二步正好说明了 Lean 的用处：一离开能模拟的门集，就只剩证明能确认它是对的。
- 聚变：把电子用量子傅里叶变换搬到实空间网格上算相互作用，并利用泡利不相容原理。量子行走的步数降了 12.8 倍，代价是每步 T 门变成 1.42 倍。另外用一个 42 比特寄存器保留总动量，每步 T 门又省 10%。
- 光化学：用测量反计算坐标，代替原来的 swap；用 Bernstein 多项式在期望意义下得到 1/r，省掉乘法；核电荷直接写死。
- P450：用 one-hot 寄存器代替 QROM 查表，每步 T 门的节省有 95% 以上来自这一招。
- Grover「找全部」：一个新的相干机制，在 m 元候选集的叠加上沿 Johnson 图做量子行走。

这些招数单拿出来，量子算法研究者大多不陌生，换坐标系、用测量代替反计算、查表换编码，都是常见手法。我觉得智能体的价值在于：它们能在一个具体问题上把这些手法大量组合、逐个证完，人很难有这个耐心。

## 和其他「AI 发现算法」的做法对比

这项工作 | AlphaEvolve 类数值搜索 | AlphaProof Code（11 月） | Axiom 形式化 CFSG（10 月） 
---|---|---|---
目标 | 发现更便宜的新程序 | 发现更好的算法 / 构造 | 证明已有代码安全 | 形式化已有定理

这几项都把「可信」交给证明器，智能体负责搜索；只要守门的检查器够严，智能体怎么试都行。这次的不同在于，前几项要么是证已有的东西，要么是能运行的对象；这次是在一个没法运行、只能靠证明的领域里找新东西。

## 局限：要打折看的地方

1. 基线是作者调整过的。 P450 的基线在已发表结果上合并了后续的编译改进（大约减半），又从只求基态扩展到 0.1 Ha 以内所有本征态，成本因此加了 0.85%。光化学用的是原作者后续工作的改进版。聚变基线是作者按原文公式和参数自己重算的。这些调整方向上多数是把基线做强，比较算公平，但读者没法直接拿原论文的数字核对。

2. 证明的是「满足规范」，不是「解决了科学问题」。 规范本身做了简化，比如聚变模型里 216 个质子被当成经典量。规范写错了或者简化过头，Lean 照样会通过。研究者只需要审规范，这是优点，同时也意味着整件事的可信度落在那几百行规范上。

3. 没有任何一个电路在硬件上跑过。 官方原话是，即便有了这些改进，真实科学模拟需要的资源仍然超过第一代纠错量子计算机可能提供的水平。成本降 11.8 倍，不代表比特数降 11.8 倍，更不代表聚变研究变便宜了。

4. 同一个结果有几种说法。 聚变：博客 11.8×，论文表 11.8×，Pushmeet Kohli 在 X 上说 10.9×，DeepMind 官方账号说「最多 10 倍」；光化学：8× / 8.1× / 8.22×。没人解释差异，我猜是口径不同（比如是否含某些子程序），但这只是推测。

5. 协调系统没开源，算力没公开。 能复现的是「这些程序确实被证明了」，不能复现的是「智能体怎么找到它们」。跑了多久、用了多少算力，我在论文正文里没找到（可能在附录，本文未核实）。

6. 没有外部专家评价。 目前的报道基本都在转述官方说法。量子算法圈对这几个基线选得对不对、改进有没有被已有工作覆盖，还要等同行看。

## 我的判断

我觉得这篇最有分量的部分是那个 Lean 库，290 倍反而其次。量子算法研究长期缺一个能「机器检查」的地基，论文、讲义里的资源估算往往是手算加经验，出错了也很难发现。现在有了带资源计数的量子 Hoare 逻辑，加上一套开源的规范和已验证解，以后谁说「我把某算法成本降了 X 倍」，都可以要求他给出 Lean 证明。这对人类研究者同样有用。

至于智能体本身，我的看法稍微保守一点。它们找到的改进都是已知技巧的新组合，还谈不上新的算法思想。但「已知技巧在具体问题上大规模组合并证完」本来就是量子资源估算领域最耗人的部分，过去一篇论文做一个分子要花几个月。这部分被机器接过去，研究者就能把时间花在挑问题和写规范上，这正是博客里说的分工。

最近几周，「AI 搜索 + 形式化验证」的项目接连出现，从数学证明到软件安全再到量子算法，路线越来越一致：人写规范，智能体干活，证明器守门。这条路线能走多远，取决于规范这一层能不能也被检查，目前还只能靠人。

# DeepMind's Gemini 4 Quantum Results: What the Lean Proofs Verify

Read the formal specification, cost model and hardware caveats behind DeepMind's reported quantum circuit improvements.

Google DeepMind's November 23 write-up explains how Gemini 4 agent teams proposed cheaper quantum circuits and checked them with Lean. The underlying preprint was first posted November 6. The practical value of the public materials is that you can inspect what the proof says and what the cost comparison assumes.

If you saw the reported 290× improvement for an arcsine routine, start with the noun: it is a result for a particular quantum arithmetic routine against a baseline. It is not a 290× measurement on a quantum computer or a speedup for every program that uses arcsine.

## Start with the specification

The researchers set the tasks and used Gemini agents to search among possible circuits. A circuit is a sequence of quantum operations. In the paper's setup, an agent has to justify that the sequence meets a mathematical specification before its result can count. The authors describe separate teams sharing checked ideas and discussing approaches in periodic meetings.

Open the public Lean repository and look for the problem specification before the proposed implementation. The main branch separates the library for quantum reasoning and resource counting from the specifications and challenge definitions. The README points to a separatediscoveries branch for the paper's programs.

A proof is only as useful as its target. For a numerical routine, look for the permitted input range, the allowed error and what the circuit must leave unchanged. If you plan to reuse the result with broader input conditions or tighter accuracy, the old proof doesn't automatically carry over.

## Read the resource comparison separately

A quantum algorithm can be correct and still be too costly to run. The paper's arithmetic section counts 3,698 T gates and 100 logical qubits for the final arcsine circuit, then multiplies those counts to get a cost score of 369,800. The baseline's score exceeds 108 million under the authors' accounting, and the baseline and new circuit report different error tolerances. The separate 2.57× parallel-search result counts expected oracle rounds, meaning calls to a function that marks targets. The two headline numbers measure different things.

Then look for what sits outside the model. For example, the library README describes more explicit models for classical control and computation as future work. An estimated reduction in logical quantum resources doesn't tell you exactly how long the computation takes on a particular machine, where error correction, measurement, routing and classical coordination affect the result.

## Ask what it would take to use the building block

For an easy paper-reading exercise, write down two lines for the arcsine example: what the circuit promises to compute and what the table counts. Then add a third: where in your own application that work would happen. If the optimized routine accounts for a small share of the full cost, even a large reduction in that component can have little effect on the complete workload.

That also gives you a fair comparison with other AI-assisted circuit papers. A sampled test can be useful when finding candidates. A formal proof gives a different kind of evidence for the modeled statement. Neither establishes that the circuit ran on hardware. DeepMind itself says the scientific simulations discussed in the announcement still exceed the expected resources of early error-corrected machines.

The useful advance is that a proposed improvement comes with a statement you can inspect instead of a speedup you have to take on trust. Check the statement and the accounting before you use the number.

I'm Paras. I help technical teams explain research with enough detail for a reader to judge the evidence. Book a 30-minute call.

# Google DeepMind Gemini 4 Agents Cut Quantum Compute Costs by Up to 10.9x

From marketbrief.now

Gemini 4 agents from Google DeepMind identified new quantum algorithms that reduce estimated compute costs by 10.9x for fusion simulations and 8.1x for photochemistry. In simulations of Cytochrome P450, an enzyme used in drug metabolism, the agents found a 2.5x improvement and reduced required memory from 481 to 333 qubits.

The team used the Lean theorem prover to mathematically verify each quantum circuit result. Google DeepMind noted that while these efficiency gains are promising, practical quantum simulations will require more powerful hardware than first-generation error-corrected machines.

- 科学发现：材料方向连续自主运行 48 小时，从 270 万个候选分子中筛选目标，经 4 轮设计—合成—测试闭环，真实合成出一种新型冷却液材料；药物方向针对阿尔兹海默症关键靶点完成 454 次工具调用与 3239 项计算评估，优化 24 个候选分子，优选分子与靶点的名义结合亲和力较起点提高约 3.6 倍。

制造业里的对比更直观：在汽车产线规划、零件设计与加工验证流程中，单个工件加工编程的人工耗时从 475 分钟压缩到 24 分钟。反过来，简单问答、轻量文案这类任务用不上旗舰档位，选更小的模型更划算。想按自己的业务模态和任务类型挑模型，可以在阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面上直接筛选对比。

## 六、接入方式：三步跑通，Token Plan 是当下主通道

对开发者而言，最关心的是能不能马上用上。当前接入路径已经比较清晰：登录阿里云百炼控制台完成实名认证，在模型广场确认 Qwen4-Max 的可用状态，创建并获取 API Key，再把 Base URL 与模型名替换为对应配置即可发起请求。

平台提供兼容 OpenAI 协议的标准化接口，原有业务代码仅需少量配置修改就能平滑迁移。同时提供独占吞吐 DTU 能力、RAG 知识库、MCP 插件托管、SFT / DPO / LoRA 等多种微调方式，以及企业级 VPC 隔离与数据加密。

计费上有两条线值得留意：一是模型调用侧的限时折扣，预览窗口期内调用 qwen4-max-preview 按标准费率的 20% 计费，该窗口按官方说明截至 11 月 25 日 24:00（UTC+8）；二是 Token Plan 订阅，采用 Credits 统一计量，一份额度覆盖平台内多款模型，个人版分 Lite、Essential、Standard、Pro 四档，团队版以坐席为单位采购，支持额度分配与成员权限管理，新客首购 5 折活动持续至 11 月 30 日。

- 个人尝鲜：Lite 档 39 元 / 月，5 折后 19.5 元 / 月，含 20000 Credits，支持 1—2 个 Agent 并发。
- 进阶开发：Essential 档 79 元 / 月，折后 39.5 元 / 月，含 45000 Credits，并发上限更高。
- 团队协作：团队版按坐席订阅，提供 198 元 / 698 元 / 1398 元三档，对应 25000 / 100000 / 250000 Credits 月度额度。

具体档位、优惠期限与区域差异会随时调整，下单前建议对照阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面的最新说明，同时做好 API Key 安全管控与用量告警。

## 结语

Qwen4-Max 这一代的看点，不在单项能力刷榜，而在"更长的上下文、更少的 Token、更低的单任务成本、能交付成果的执行方式"这四件事同时往前走。选型逻辑可以先看任务是否需要长链路与工具协同：需要，就上旗舰；不需要，就用更小的模型省钱。要把这些能力真正落到业务里，阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面仍然是最快的起点。

# 最新阿里云 Qwen4‑Max 预览版深度解析：能力特性、功能介绍、选型场景、价格活动

2026-11-24 1

举报

简介： 推荐最佳实践流程：首先领取百炼新用户免费Tokens，使用自身真实业务完成适配验证，评估模型能力是否满足业务需求；确认适配之后，按需订阅Token Plan个人版或者团队版，利用预览窗口期完成压测，记录Credits消耗、任务成功率，为后续正式版上线做好技术与预算储备。选型时遵循业务场景匹配原则，简单任务选择Flash或者Plus，复杂长链路任务才启用Qwen4‑Max，兼顾业务效果与使用成本。

2026年11月阿里云正式对外发布通义千问第四代旗舰大模型Qwen4‑Max预览版，在千问AI平台首发上线Token Plan订阅服务。该模型作为Qwen4系列的最高规格旗舰档位，定位面向复杂专业任务的高性能AI引擎，具备1M Token上下文窗口，原生支持文本、图片、视频三模态输入，重点强化复杂编程、智能体长链路任务、专业办公处理三大方向。现阶段预览版仅开放订阅制调用，不支持传统按量计费模式，预览窗口期为2026年11月11日10:00至11月25日24:00（UTC+8），窗口期结束之后qwen4‑max‑preview模型标识将直接下线，正式版会采用全新模型名称对外发布，开发者需要提前预留接口配置修改的工作量。截至预览版发布，官方尚未对外披露完整参数规模、正式版定价以及开源相关规划。在优惠层面，新用户可以先领取超7000万免费Tokens完成业务效果验证，再参与Token Plan新客5折活动，Lite档位低至19.5元每月，叠加Qwen4‑Max预览版限时2折调用折扣之后，最低可以做到原价1折体验新一代旗舰模型能力。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

## 一、Qwen4‑Max大模型是什么

Qwen4‑Max是阿里云通义千问Qwen家族第四代旗舰大模型，本次对外开放的为预览版本，模型标识qwen4‑max‑preview。“Max”代表同代产品当中性能天花板，预览版则代表该版本主要用于能力验证、收集真实用户反馈，模型逻辑在窗口期内保持稳定，方便开发者开展统一基准测试，但并不适合直接承接7×24小时不间断的生产业务。

从家族产品矩阵来看，Qwen4系列规划多款主力型号，覆盖旗舰性能档、综合均衡档、高速低成本档位以及面向本地部署的中等参数版本。Qwen4‑Max并不以日常闲聊对话作为核心目标，核心定位是处理高复杂度、长链路、多工具协同的专业工作任务，阿里云百炼平台也将该模型归类到“复杂推理与编程”分类之下。

在产品体验入口上，Qwen4‑Max预览版首发依托Token Plan订阅服务，同时打通千问办公、Qoder、千问APP、QwenStudio四大产品入口。普通用户更新千问APP之后，即可切换模型完成对话体验；开发者与企业用户既可以通过API完成程序调用，也可以直接使用上层应用开展工作。简单来说，Qwen4‑Max不是一款优化日常聊天体验的对话模型，而是面向真实业务的高性能任务处理引擎，它的核心追求不是“回答问题好听”，而是“完整把复杂任务做完”。

## 二、Qwen4‑Max大模型核心能力

官方将Qwen4‑Max的升级归纳为四大方向，分别是知识理解、世界感知、编程能力、Agentic智能体任务执行，其中编程开发与智能体长链路执行是本次迭代的两大核心重点。相较于上一代Qwen3‑Max，模型评价重心从单轮问答质量转向端到端任务完成成功率。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

编程能力：模型支持大型完整项目代码生成、代码仓库级审计、项目架构重构、漏洞排查修复。不仅可以输出业务逻辑代码，还能够直接生成前端交互网页、3D建模脚本、软件自动化操作脚本，自动完成报错调试、单元测试补全、项目配套文档撰写。内测阶段已经完成大量3D建模、网页交互开发场景验证，同时Qoder编程平台已经完成预览版的全量接入，Teams、Enterprise企业套餐均可直接使用该模型开展开发工作。

Agentic智能体能力：面对复杂业务目标，模型可以自主拆解任务步骤，分轮次调用联网搜索、代码解释器、文件处理等各类工具，降低人工干预的频次。针对长周期业务任务，减少执行中途断链、陷入无效循环等常见问题，适合搭建科研流水线、财务自动化分析、多步骤办公机器人等复杂智能体业务。

知识理解与世界感知能力：区别于传统模型简单复述静态知识库内容，Qwen4‑Max强化动态世界信息理解能力，完成文本、图像、结构化数据之间深度语义对齐。处理物理常识、社会逻辑、跨领域专业知识时，可以构建更长的因果推理链条，主动识别问题内部隐含前提，修正错误假设。

长上下文与多模态输入能力：预览版支持100万Token上下文窗口，输入格式包含文本、图片、视频，输出格式为文本。视觉输入规格上，单张图片最高支持1600万像素，视频最长支持2小时，单个视频文件上限2GB。开发者可以直接上传截图、图表文档、视频素材，模型统一完成解析，无需拆分交由多个不同模型处理。需要注意，参数规模、开源计划官方暂未公示，网络流传相关信息没有官方背书，选型工作必须以阿里云官网模型列表页面为准。

## 三、Qwen4‑Max大模型主要功能

Qwen4‑Max预览版全部功能围绕工具调用、流程可控、业务系统对接三大目标设计，提供丰富工程化能力，降低业务落地的开发成本。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

第一，原生函数调用与内置工具。完整支持Function Calling函数调用，自带联网搜索、网页抓取、代码解释器等内置工具，为搭建多工具协同工作流提供底层基础。

第二，标准化结构化输出。支持JSON Object、JSON Schema两种结构化输出模式，模型输出结果可以直接对接下游业务系统，省去大量文本后处理开发工作。

第三，可调强度深度思考模式。模型默认开启深度思考，开发者可以通过参数调整推理力度，在输出精度和响应速度之间灵活取舍，适配不同业务场景需求。这里存在一处极易踩坑的技术细节：从该预览版本开始，max_tokens和max_completion_tokens统计范围同时包含思考推理过程内容 + 最终输出回答内容。如果沿用旧版本调用习惯，只为最终回答分配Token额度，长推理任务就会发生输出提前截断，造成业务异常。

第四，强大多模态理解。直接解析网页截图、图表文档、视频素材，图文、视频混合的业务资料无需预处理拆分。

第五，多套主流API接口兼容。原生兼容OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses以及Anthropic Messages接口格式，原有基于这两套接口开发的业务，修改Base URL与模型ID即可完成迁移，改造成本较低。

第六，多元化交互入口。除标准API调用之外，开发者、办公人员、普通用户还可以分别使用Qoder、千问办公、千问APP、QwenStudio开展测试使用。

## 四、Qwen4‑Max大模型适用场景

结合官方定位与早期内测反馈，Qwen4‑Max预览版更加适配结果质量要求高、执行流程长、步骤繁多的复杂任务。

复杂编程开发场景：全栈项目代码生成、仓库级代码审计与架构重构、前端交互页面开发、3D建模脚本编写、软件自动化流程搭建，适合独立开发者、研发团队开展大型工程项目。

多步骤Agent智能体场景：需要多轮工具协同、自主拆解业务目标的长周期任务，例如科研数据处理流水线、财务自动分析系统、办公自动化机器人等智能体业务。

长文档和混合资料分析场景：一次性读取几十万字合同、完整书籍、整套代码库，完成合同条款比对、风险识别、内容归纳总结；同时支持图文表格、视频混合材料的联合研判分析。

专业办公与软件自动化场景：财报深度解读、法律合同审阅、行业调研报告撰写、专业软件操作自动化，面向企业法务、财务、行业研究人员。

同时也存在不适合使用该旗舰预览版的业务：高并发、低延迟、成本敏感的简单问答、普通文案生成。这类业务选择Qwen4‑Flash、Qwen4‑Plus性价比更高。应当遵循“旗舰模型处理旗舰任务”原则，避免大模型能力浪费，控制整体AI调用成本。另外预览版本身不适合生产业务，正式商用必须等待正式版本发布。

## 五、Qwen4‑Max大模型收费标准

Qwen4‑Max预览版仅开放Token Plan订阅模式调用，不支持普通按量付费接口。开发者需要先订阅Token Plan套餐，通过套餐内统一计量单位Credits消耗模型调用资源，一套订阅额度可以在千问系列多款模型、配套工具之间通用。2026年11月9日官方完成套餐额度调整，个人版四档套餐详情如下：

套餐档位 | 官网原价 | 每月Credits | 备注 
---|---|---|---
Lite | 39元/月 | 20000 | 新客首购5折后19.5元/月 
Essential | 79元/月 | 45000 | 新客首购5折后39.5元/月 
Standard | 139元/月 | 80000 | 附赠Harness工具权益 
Pro | 312元/月 | 200000 | 附赠Harness工具权益 

团队版按照座席进行计费，双11限时活动价格：标准座席150元/座席/月、高级座席550元/座席/月、尊享座席1398元/座席/月，原价更高；团队可以额外购买共享用量包，供给全部团队成员共同使用。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

费用抵扣存在固定优先级顺序：免费额度 → 资源包 → 节省计划 → 按量付费。Token Plan套餐内Credits额度按月重置，当月未使用完毕额度不会结转至下个月。套餐Credits耗尽之后，可以单独购买用量包补充额度，个人版用量包100元每个，包含20000 Credits，账号最多同时持有5个用量包。Standard及以上档位附赠Harness工具权益，联网搜索、网页解析、图像生成、代码解释器、知识库沙箱等工具调用不会消耗Credits，将工具类任务交给Harness处理，Credits全部留给模型推理，可以进一步降低整体使用成本。

## 六、Qwen4‑Max大模型便宜购买方法

想要把使用成本控制在合理区间，整套流程分为两步，优先使用免费额度验证业务适配性，再利用订阅折扣压低长期调用成本。

### 6.1 充分利用新用户免费试用额度

完成实名认证、首次开通阿里云百炼服务的新用户，可以领取超7000万免费Tokens；完成企业认证的账号累计可以领取1亿以上Tokens。每一款主流模型分配约100万独立Tokens，千问对话、代码、多模态模型均可覆盖。

使用规则需要重点留意：额度有效期90天，仅限华北2（北京）地域，其他地域无法抵扣；额度不会注册自动下发，必须在百炼控制台开通服务并且切换至华北2地域，通常两小时内完成发放；免费额度只支持实时推理API调用和控制台对话，不能用于批量任务、模型微调、私有化部署；主账号和RAM子账号共用同一额度池。建议开启“用完即停”防护，某一个模型免费额度耗尽之后系统不会自动切换其他模型继续运行，避免意外产生按量计费账单。

### 6.2 Token Plan订阅方案选型

Token Plan是阿里云百炼推出按月付费AI订阅服务，使用统一Credits计量调用资源，不用为不同模型、不同工具单独充值记账。传统按量付费模式，当工具、模型数量变多，账单预测、对账难度会大幅上升；Token Plan将单次调用计费转变为固定月费换取月度额度，预算可控，叠加大促折扣之后单位调用成本优于按量付费。额度耗尽后补充用量包，同样比溢出后直接按量计费更加划算。

个人版优惠规则：Token Plan新用户首购享受5折优惠，Lite档位19.5元每月、Essential档位39.5元每月；5折权益仅限从未购买过Token Plan个人版的账号，同一个实名主体只能享受一次，活动有效期截止2026年11月30日23:59:59。在此基础之上Qwen4‑Max预览版限时调用2折，两项折扣叠加最低实现原价1折体验。

### 6.3 重要风险提示

# 2026 年 Qwen4-Max 是什么模型？能力边界与落地场景一次讲清

2026-11-24 2

举报

简介： Qwen4-Max 是 2026年 Qwen4 系列的旗舰基座，2.4T 总参数、71B 激活、原生视觉、百万 Token 上下文，配合 GDN 与 QSA 混合注意力把长上下文的读取成本压了下来。它的价值不在单点分数，而在"能把长任务跑完并交付成品"这件事上，同时把单任务成本拉低了近六成。适用边界也很清楚：需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，当前并不适用。选型时先看任务形态，再看成本结构，比只看榜单分数更有意义。

2026年11月，阿里云正式发布通义千问新一代旗舰基座模型 Qwen4-Max，并同步上线百炼平台。与前代旗舰相比，这一代的重点不再是单项能力刷榜，而是把优化方向压在专业工作场景的长链路任务上：更长的上下文、更少的 Token 消耗、更低的单任务成本，以及能持续交付可用成果的执行方式。本文从模型定位、架构特征、能力清单、评测表现、适用场景、接入方式六个层面做完整解析。文中数据取自官方模型卡与公开评测材料，具体规格以百炼模型页实时信息为准。

## 一、模型定位：从问答工具转向可交付工作的基座

Qwen4-Max 的官方定位是新一代旗舰多模态智能体基座模型。它的设计假设很明确：企业里真正有价值的工作，很少能塞进一次对话。这些任务往往持续数小时、跨越几十个工具、涉及上千页资料，最终必须产出一份团队能直接使用的东西——一份可运行的代码、一份可评审的方案、一张可交付的设计稿。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

因此它的能力取向围绕三件事展开：第一，能稳定调用专业工具链，而不只是生成文本；第二，能把长任务推进到终点，中途不丢上下文、不跑偏；第三，交付的是成品而非中间回答。官方把这套机制命名为 Live Delivery（渐进交付）：在长任务开始时先给出一版可用的初版，之后持续迭代提交改进版本，让团队在任务运行过程中就能评审和纠偏，而不是等到最后才发现方向错了。

这一定位决定了它与轻量对话模型的分工。日常问答、简单文案，用更小的模型成本更低；而跨文档分析、多文件工程改造、长流程智能体，才是 Qwen4-Max 的合理使用区间。

## 二、架构特征：2.4T 参数与百万上下文如何兼顾效率

Qwen4-Max 总参数规模为 2.4 万亿（2.4T），单 Token 仅激活 710 亿（71B），另外配置 3280 亿（328B）的 N-gram Embedding 参数。总参数大、激活参数小，是典型的稀疏混合专家路线，目的是在保住能力上限的同时压住单次推理的算力开销。官方数据显示，每个 Token 的激活参数比上一代减少约 25%。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

支撑百万级上下文的，是三项架构改动：

GDN + QSA 混合注意力。 每四层中，三层使用 Gated DeltaNet（GDN），把历史信息压缩成固定大小的状态，使 KV 缓存不随上下文长度线性增长；剩下一层使用 Qwen Sparse Attention（QSA），通过轻量索引定位关键段落。官方给出的效果是百万 Token 读取速度提升 7 倍以上。这一点对长文档、长代码库场景意义很大——上下文再长，显存与延迟也不会失控。

GR 门控残差。 把单通道残差流展宽为 4 条并行分支，配合动态读写门控，增强跨层信息传递。工程上的直接收益是 2.4T 规模训练全程平稳，没有出现损失突增（Loss Spike）。这类改动不出现在能力指标里，但决定了大模型能否稳定训到目标规模。

N-gram Embedding。 单独配置 328B 的 N-gram 嵌入参数，用于强化高频片段的表征，对代码、术语密集的专业文本有直接帮助。

规格层面，Qwen4-Max 上下文长度为 100 万 Token，最大输入 991,808 Token，最大输出 131,072 Token；开启思考模式时，最大输入 983,616 Token、最大输出 262,144 Token，最大思维链长度同为 262,144 Token。输入模态覆盖文本、图像、视频，输出为文本。原生视觉并非后期拼接的适配层，工程图纸、医疗影像、长视频都可以直接作为输入。

## 三、能力清单：哪些能做，哪些不做

官方模型卡列出的支持项包括：流式输出、深度思考、并行工具调用、联网搜索、前缀补全、Function Calling、思维链摘要与加密、结构化输出（JSON Object 与 JSON Schema）、显式缓存与隐式缓存、批量推理。接口层面兼容 OpenAI Chat Completions、Responses、Anthropic Messages 与 DashScope，迁移成本较低，已有 OpenAI 或 Anthropic 风格调用的项目大多只需换 Base URL 与模型 ID。

深度思考默认开启，可通过 reasoning_effort 调节推理力度。这里有一个必须注意的工程细节：从预览版开始，max_tokens 与 max_completion_tokens 语义等价，二者共同限制"思考内容 + 最终回答"的总量。如果沿用过去只为回答预留上限的写法，开启思考后输出会被提前截断。迁移时应当为思考与回答共同预留额度。

明确不支持的项同样重要：模型调优不支持，模型部署不支持。也就是说，Qwen4-Max 只能以 API 方式调用，不能私有化微调后自行部署。对数据必须留在自有环境的项目，这条限制需要在选型阶段就确认清楚。

## 四、评测表现：能力提升与成本下降同时发生

官方公布的 Work360 评测中，Qwen4-Max 得分 52.69，上一代为 47.74。在相同推理力度下，单任务 Token 消耗明显下降：Work360 在 Xhigh 与 High 两档分别减少约 24% 与 35%，Terminal-Bench 4.0 分别减少约 48% 与 49%。综合结果是平均单任务成本比上一代下降 58%。详情👉访问阿里云百炼大模型服务平台页面 了解。

中文通用能力侧，2026年11月的 SuperCLUE 测评中 Qwen4-Max 取得 61.61 分，进入国内第一梯队，较上一版本提升 18.39 分。分项上，幻觉控制 73.61 分、提升 40.56 分；超长上下文 77.80 分、提升 33.42 分；智能体编程 57.69 分、提升 15.38 分。更值得关注的是稳定性：上一代在同一测试中超时率为 69.23%，新模型超时率降至 0%，全部试题跑完。按测试的 Token 开销与定价折算，平均每题成本约 1.90 元，较上一代下降约 87%。

这组数据的含义是：能力提升之外，单位任务的调用成本出现了数量级变化。对高频跑智能体流程的团队来说，成本项的变化往往比分数更能决定项目是否跑得起来。

## 五、适用场景：六类任务最匹配

编程开发与工程改造。 支持多文件读取、工具调用与结构化输出，配合百万上下文可直接把整个代码库放进一次会话。Terminal-Bench 上 Token 消耗下降近半，意味着批量重构、批量测试生成这类任务的账单压力明显减轻。

前端与设计还原。 原生视觉可直接读取设计稿、截图、原型图，输出可运行的页面代码，适合设计到开发的衔接环节。

办公与文档处理。 长报告、合同、财报、会议材料，单份即可覆盖在上下文内，不需要切块摘要再拼接，减少信息在切分过程中丢失的问题。结构化输出可以直接产出 JSON，方便对接下游系统。

复杂智能体与流程自动化。 并行工具调用、联网搜索、Function Calling 齐备，适合需要串联检索、计算、写文件、调用内部接口的长链路流程。Live Delivery 机制让长任务可以边跑边交付，便于中途校正。

专业视觉理解。 工程图纸、医疗影像、长视频分析，属于原生视觉的典型用例，无需额外接视觉模型。

长文档审阅与合规核查。 幻觉控制分项的大幅提升，加上长上下文能力，适合条款比对、事实核验这类对准确性敏感的工作。

反过来，不适合的场景也要说清：单轮简单问答、短文案润色、固定模板填表，用旗舰模型的成本没有必要；需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，Qwen4-Max 目前不提供这两条路径。

## 六、接入与计费：Token Plan 是唯一入口

Qwen4-Max 通过百炼接入，预览版 qwen4-max-preview 仅支持 Token Plan，不开放按量计费。预览期为 2026年11月11日 10:00 至 11月25日 24:00（UTC+8），期间模型能力持续迭代，预览结束后下线，正式版 qwen4-max 已上线，建议直接使用正式版。

调用方式上，先开通 Token Plan 个人版或团队版，获取套餐专用 API Key（前缀 sk-sp），使用套餐专用 Base URL：
export DASHSCOPE_API_KEY="sk-sp-xxxxxxxx"
export BASE_URL="[https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com](https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com)"

          AI 代码解读

以 OpenAI 兼容方式发起一次带思考的调用：
curl "$BASE_URL/compatible-mode/v1/chat/completions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $DASHSCOPE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "qwen4-max",
    "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "分析这份接口文档的字段变更风险"}],
    "reasoning_effort": "high",
    "max_completion_tokens": 8192
  }'

          AI 代码解读

用 SDK 时同样只需替换模型与地址：
from openai import OpenAI

client = OpenAI(
    api_key="sk-sp-xxxxxxxx",
    base_url="[https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1](https://token-plan.cn-beijing.maas.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1)",
)
resp = client.chat.completions.create(
    model="qwen4-max",
    messages=[{
   "role": "user", "content": "把这段 SQL 改写成可并行的版本"}],
    reasoning_effort="high",
    max_completion_tokens=8192,
)
print(resp.choices[0].message.content)

          AI 代码解读

计费侧需要记住三点：Token Plan 以 Credits 统一计量，一份订阅额度可覆盖平台内多款模型，套餐额度按月重置、不结转；套餐专用 Key 与通用 Key、其他订阅计划不通用；部署地域为华北2（北京），跨境业务需评估访问链路。

## 七、选型建议

判断是否需要 Qwen4-Max，可以先回答三个问题：任务是否需要跨几十页文档或整个代码库？是否需要在一次会话里连续调用多个工具直到产出成品？是否对事实准确性高度敏感？三项中命中两项以上，旗舰档才值得；否则更小的模型配外部工具组合，性价比通常更好。

对已经在用上一代旗舰的团队，迁移的收益主要落在两处：单任务 Token 消耗下降带来的账单缩减，以及超时率归零带来的流程稳定性。迁移风险集中在输出预算参数——务必按"思考 + 回答"合计的口径重新设定上限，否则会出现长任务被截断、看起来像模型能力不足的误判。

## 八、总结

Qwen4-Max 是 2026年 Qwen4 系列的旗舰基座，2.4T 总参数、71B 激活、原生视觉、百万 Token 上下文，配合 GDN 与 QSA 混合注意力把长上下文的读取成本压了下来。它的价值不在单点分数，而在"能把长任务跑完并交付成品"这件事上，同时把单任务成本拉低了近六成。适用边界也很清楚：需要私有化部署或模型微调的项目，当前并不适用。选型时先看任务形态，再看成本结构，比只看榜单分数更有意义。

# China’s Z.ai ‘aggressively’ using looped transformer method to improve AI models

Company is first Chinese firm to disclose using emerging technique, which offers performance gains but also raises safety concerns

2-MIN READ2-MIN

0

Listen

Chinese artificial intelligence company Z.ai has credited an emerging technique – one that has drawn scrutiny from AI safety researchers – with helping its newly released flagship model achieve significant performance gains over its predecessor while improving computational efficiency.

The release marks the first time a Chinese AI company has disclosed using a “looped transformer” architecture in a major model, following recent reports that US giant OpenAI adopted the same method for its newest models.

In a blog post, Z.ai, also known as Zhipu AI, said it “aggressively” applied the technique over the past three months, enabling its GLM-5.4 model to match the performance of AI models two to four times its size.

“This lets us raise the intelligence ceiling with a relatively small compute overhead,” the company said, noting that the technique drove improvements in mathematics, science and coding, though it withheld the detailed benchmark scores typically published alongside major model releases.

While standard transformers, the dominant architecture behind AI breakthroughs in recent years, process new data through each layer of its internal neural network once, a looped transformer passes data through the same layers multiple times.

This creates a deeper reasoning network without substantially increasing parameter count or computing costs.

That efficiency offers an edge as the global AI industry races towards massive, trillion-parameter models, which tend to deliver stronger capabilities but are vastly more expensive to train and run.

YouTube video player

Unlike domestic rivals such as Moonshot AI and DeepSeek, Z.ai has yet to release a flagship trillion-parameter model. GLM-5.4 retains the same 750-billion-parameter size as its predecessor, GLM-5.3, but performs at a level equivalent to a model in the 2 trillion to 3 trillion parameter range, according to Z.ai.

A significant scale-up also appears to be imminent. Z.ai hinted on Monday that its next model would be “significantly larger” and ready “soon”.

That aligns with a JPMorgan research note published last week, which cited an internal road map shared by Z.ai management indicating GLM-5.4 would be used to “verify training performance” ahead of a 3-trillion-parameter release by year-end aimed at “reaching the global frontier”.

Despite its efficiency gains, the looped transformer method has sparked debate over AI safety oversight and the risks of “black box” systems escaping human control.

Conventional reasoning models “think” out loud in human-readable text before generating a final answer or action, allowing researchers to monitor their logic for unwanted behaviour such as deception.

Because looped transformers reuse parts of internal neural layers, safety experts warn that a model’s decision-making process can become hidden inside those loops, making it largely opaque to human researchers.

Z.ai said GLM-5.4 spent fewer tokens on visible “thinking”, with average output length dropping up to 14 per cent on key benchmarks. “In effect, part of the reasoning shifts from explicit output tokens into the implicit depth of the loop,” the blog post said.

The safety debate gained momentum in September after US tech outlet The Information reported that OpenAI’s flagship GPT-6 Astra model would, for the first time, rely on a looped transformer to boost performance without inflating costs.

OpenAI did not confirm the report, though chief scientist Jakub Pachocki acknowledged safety concerns in subsequent social media posts, with a company representative calling the decline in model transparency “a real challenge that [it] takes seriously”.

Z.ai signalled similar caution on Monday. The company has restricted access to GLM-5.4 to its official chatbot website and coding service, saying it planned to open-source the model at an unspecified date “after completing necessary safety hardening”.

# Z.ai's GLM-5.4 aims to match models up to four times its size by running 28 layers twice

Z.ai's main evidence for the claim comes from a 30B test model, and early testers say the looped model is slow but useful for hunting bugs and security flaws.

GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first flagship built on a Loop Transformer architecture, which reuses the same layers more than once instead of stacking new ones, so the model gets more depth and more computation per token without adding parameters. Thinking Machines Lab used a looped transformer in its Inkling 2 Mini model, which was released last week.

The GLM-5.4 model also adds vision and targets what Z.ai calls Generalized Coding, which applies code to engineering and design work such as mechanical design and 3D modeling, not only to software. GLM-5.4 follows GLM-5.3, which Z.ai released in August with advanced cyber capabilities.

GLM-5.4 is available now through Z.ai's GLM Coding Plan, ZCode and Z.ai Chat. API access is listed as coming soon, and Z.ai says open weights will follow after safety hardening, with no date given.

Z.ai has published a win-rate chart comparing GLM-5.4 with three other models, but without explaining the evaluation methodology. Its main controlled benchmark evidence comes from a separate test using a 30B model, and it acknowledges that GLM-5.4 can get caught in overly long reasoning loops.

## How GLM-5.4 works: 28 layers run twice instead of adding parameters

Z.ai describes large-scale software engineering, cybersecurity, 3D modeling and physical control as ultra-long-chain reasoning tasks, which require following multi-step causal chains while keeping global logical consistency.

"Stacking parameters and memorizing data cannot solve this," Z.ai said.

Conventional Transformers process each layer once per forward pass. GLM-5.4 instead sends intermediate representations through the same group of layers twice, increasing computational depth without adding parameters.

Researchers explored layer reuse in the 2018 Universal Transformer, although much of the subsequent work has focused on smaller models.

GLM-5.4 loops 28 layers of the GLM-5 base for two iterations at the 750B scale, adapted from an already pre-trained model through continued training.

Looping carries costs of its own, so Z.ai made three architectural changes to balance performance against deployment cost.

Gated progressive updates. Repeatedly updating the model's internal representations can cause instability. Z.ai says GLM-5.4 uses per-token gates to control how much each iteration changes them.

Z.ai reports that after training the first pass builds global context and writes conservatively. The second pass opens the gates to write full updates. The gates also adjust step size by token difficulty, so harder tokens get more aggressive first-pass writes.

Hybrid KV cache. Rather than maintaining a complete KV cache for each iteration, GLM-5.4 reuses the first pass's sparse KV cache and limits additional storage to a sliding window for the second pass.

Sparse attention index reuse. The second loop reuses the attention indices from the first loop's indexer, which avoids a second indexing pass. Z.ai's experiments show this performs nearly identically to recomputing indices on every pass.

## Early tests show gains on a 30B model, but questions remain about GLM-5.4's performance

Z.ai describes GLM-5.4 as reaching intelligence levels comparable to 2T-3T parameter models, but does not explain how it arrived at that comparison.

Its main controlled evidence is a 30B test model, where the looped version used about 10% more training compute than a non-looped baseline of the same size. Z.ai reports the largest improvements in math, scientific reasoning and long-context tasks, along with shorter average outputs, by about 15% on MMLU-Pro and 12% on GPQA-Diamond. Those results were measured on the smaller test model, not GLM-5.4 itself.

## Community reactions: Testers praise bug-finding and security work but flag speed and a gap to Opus 5.5

Developers who tried GLM-5.4 in its first hours report strengths in code review and security testing, and criticism over speed and rivals' lead.

In a post on X, AICodeKing placed GLM-5.4 seventh on his KingBench 4 coding benchmark. At maximum reasoning effort, GLM-5.4 took 431 minutes to complete the tests, compared with 109 minutes for Google's Gemini 4 Neon. It required 1,128 steps versus 244 for Neon.

"I wouldn't recommend you to just use this model but keeping it as a reviewer for work and making it work on more complex architecture or searching for bugs, security vulnerabilities is really worth it imo,” AICodeKing wrote.

Migel Tissera tested GLM-5.4 as a black-box attacker against a private lab environment and said it successfully completed a multistep remote code execution chain, according to his post on X.

Not every tester was persuaded.

"Sorry but GLM 5.4 is nowhere near Opus 5.5 not a single Open model is right now,” Loktar wrote on X.

Darek Gusto welcomed the built-in vision and the extra quota but noted the missing coding benchmark scores. In a post on X, Gusto wrote: "After GLM 5.4 dropped, I wanted my jaw to drop too, and it kinda did... when I realized that even in the blog there are no coding benchmarks."

A poster on Reddit r/LocalLLaMA was particularly critical of the model for any use case outside of coding. The poster also complained that the model spends half of its chain of thought wasting tokens on reasoning about whether something is OK.

## Pricing, Coding Plan and availability

GLM-5.4 is now available through the GLM Coding Plan, ZCode and Z.ai Chat. For users on weekly quota plans, Z.ai says GLM-5.4's quota is 1.5 times that of GLM-5.3.

According to Z.ai's developer documentation, GLM-5.4 accepts text, image, video and file inputs and returns text, with a 1M-token context window and a maximum output of 128K tokens. Its predecessor GLM-5.3 accepts text only. The launch post gives no vision benchmark scores.

General API pricing has not been announced. Z.ai says API access is coming soon, after it completes a security assessment. For reference, Z.ai's docs list GLM-5.3 at $1.40 per million input tokens, 26 cents for cached input and $4.40 per million output tokens. GLM-5.4 is not on that page.

Z.ai has not given a date for open weights or said which license they will carry.

"We plan to open-source the model weights responsibly after completing necessary safety hardening," the company stated.

# What Is GLM 5.4? Z.ai Loop Transformer Model Explained

GLM-5.4 is Z.ai's first Loop Transformer flagship: 750B scale, two passes over 28 GLM-5 layers, vision input, 1M context. Specs, access, limits and what is still missing.

Quick answer: GLM 5.4 (written GLM-5.4 by Z.ai) is Z.ai's newest flagship model, released on November 23, 2026. It is the company's first Loop Transformer: it runs a shared block of 28 GLM-5 base layers twice per token, at about 750B scale, and Z.ai says that reaches the level of 2T–3T parameter models. It adds vision (video, image, text and file input), keeps a 1M-token context with 128K output, and is aimed at what Z.ai calls "Generalized Coding." You can use it in Z.ai Chat, ZCode and partner coding tools. The API, open weights and benchmark scores are not out yet.

Most launch coverage repeats the "2T–3T" line and stops. This guide separates what Z.ai has actually published from what it has only claimed, so you can decide whether GLM 5.4 is worth testing now or worth waiting for.

All facts below come from Z.ai's official docs and blog, checked on November 24, 2026. If you only need the quick spec sheet and release status, our GLM 5.4 model page has it on one screen.

## TL;DR

- What it is: Z.ai's first Loop Transformer flagship, built by converting the GLM-5 base model rather than training from scratch.
- What is new: looped depth (2 passes), vision input, faster serving (up to 200 tokens/s off-peak).
- What is missing: public API, price, open weights, and any GLM 5.4 benchmark table.
- Known weakness: long "marathon thinking" on hard problems, which Z.ai itself flags.
- Where to use it: chat.z.ai, ZCode, and coding tools such as Trae, Qoder, WorkBuddy and OpenCode.

## GLM 5.4 Specs at a Glance

Spec | GLM 5.4 
---|---
Developer | Z.ai (Zhipu AI) 
Release date | November 23, 2026 
Architecture | Loop Transformer: 28 weight-shared GLM-5 layers, 2 iterations 
Scale | ~750B (active parameters not published) 
Claimed level | Comparable to 2T–3T parameter models 
Input | Video, image, text, file 
Output | Text 
Context length | 1M tokens 
Max output | 128K tokens 
Speed on Z.ai | Up to 200 tokens/s off-peak, 70–80 tokens/s at peak 
Features | Thinking mode, streaming, function calling, context caching, structured output (JSON) 
API | Coming soon, after a security assessment 
Open weights | Planned, no date 

## What Makes GLM 5.4 Different?

### 1. It loops layers instead of adding them

A normal Transformer runs each layer once per token. GLM 5.4 takes 28 layers from the GLM-5 base and runs them two times, refining the hidden state on the second pass. That makes the network deeper without adding parameters.

Z.ai's argument is that some tasks are limited by memory (they need more parameters to store facts) and others are limited by reasoning (they need more compute per step). Large software projects, security work, 3D modeling and physical control are in the second group. Looping spends more compute on each token without growing the model.

The idea is old. The 2018 Universal Transformer used shared-weight depth. What is new is doing it on a 750B production model, and doing it by continued training of an existing base instead of pretraining a looped model from scratch, which Z.ai says still lags at equal compute. Our Loop Transformer section in GLM 5.4 vs GLM 5.3 covers the three engineering changes that make it practical.

### 2. It can see

GLM 5.3 was text-only; only GLM 5.3 Flash read images. GLM 5.4 brings vision to the flagship, with video, image, text and file input. Z.ai pairs this with coding: the model reads a screenshot, a video frame or a CAD view, and then writes code against it.

### 3. "Generalized Coding"

This is Z.ai's label for using code as a general tool, not only for software. Its launch demos:

- Video: GLM 5.4 wrote code to produce and edit "Hello World," a self-narrated music video.
- Engineering: it built a 6-axis robotic arm in FreeCAD through CAD scripting.
- 3D: it generated an interactive macro bird-watching scene using math geometry and custom GLSL shaders.

These are demos picked by Z.ai, not measured results. They show the target use cases, not how often the model succeeds at them.

### 4. Shorter answers for the same reasoning

On a 30B test model with the same architecture, Z.ai reports that looping cut average output length by 10–14% on benchmarks such as GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro. Its explanation: part of the reasoning moves from visible thinking tokens into the extra loop depth. If that holds at 750B, GLM 5.4 could be cheaper per answer once it has an API price.

## What Z.ai Has Not Published

This is the part most "GLM 5.4 explained" pages skip.

Claim you may see | What Z.ai actually released 
---|---
"GLM 5.4 benchmark scores" | No public benchmark table, only an internal win-rate chart. A team member said scores will come later 
"Beats 2T–3T models" | A claim in the blog, with no named comparison models or numbers 
"GLM 5.4 API price" | No price. API waits on a security assessment 
"GLM 5.4 on Hugging Face" | No weights yet. Newest is GLM-5.3 
"GLM 5.4 Flash" | Not announced 

The docs do include a win-rate chart from Z.ai's own testing and an iso-parameter ablation at 30B. The win-rate chart is the closest thing to a head-to-head result:

GLM 5.4 vs… | Win | Tie | Lose 
---|---|---|---
GLM 5.3 | 51.1% | 25.7% | 23.1% 
Kimi K3.1 Pro | 41.8% | 26.9% | 31.3% 
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 | 36.6% | 30.2% | 33.2% 

Z.ai does not say how many tasks were used, what kind they were, or how wins were judged. So read it as "clearly ahead of GLM 5.3, modestly ahead of Kimi K3.1 Pro, roughly even with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash," not as a benchmark score. For a baseline with real numbers, see GLM 5.3 benchmarks.

Tip for testers: with no scores to compare, the most reliable signal is your own work. Run two or three real tasks you already know the answer to, and time them. Hard prompts may take noticeably longer because of the marathon-thinking issue.

## The Known Weakness: Marathon Thinking

Z.ai's own docs say GLM 5.4 "tends to get caught in overly long 'marathon thinking' loops." It also says the extra reflection "does consistently improve accuracy." In practice that means:

- simple prompts should be fine;
- hard coding or math prompts may think for a long time before answering;
- in agent tools with time or token limits, long thinking can hit those limits.

If a tool lets you lower reasoning effort, try that first on routine tasks.

## How to Use GLM 5.4 Today

- Z.ai Chat: open chat.z.ai, sign in, and pick GLM-5.4.
- ZCode: Z.ai's coding app at zcode.z.ai, for multi-step coding work.
- Partner coding tools: Trae, WorkBuddy, Qoder and OpenCode added GLM-5.4 on launch day. Pickglm-5.4 in the model menu.

It is not on OpenRouter, Ollama, Hugging Face or glm5.app yet. Our GLM 5.4 API guide explains what to do if you need programmatic access now.

## GLM 5.4 on glm5.app

glm5.app is an independent site and is not run by Z.ai. GLM 5.4 is not in our catalog yet. The flagship you can use here today is GLM 5.3, and GLM 5.3 Flash handles image input with free daily messages.

We will add GLM 5.4 once Z.ai opens its API. Check the GLM 5.4 page for status.

## Who Should Care About GLM 5.4?

- Coding agent users: the main target. Visual coding and long tasks are where Z.ai says it gained most.
- People who need vision in a GLM flagship: this is the first one.
- API builders: wait. There is no endpoint or price yet.
- Local and self-hosting users: wait for the weights, and expect hardware needs similar to other ~750B models.

## My Final Take

GLM 5.4 is an interesting architecture bet more than a proven upgrade. The design is published in unusual detail, the speed numbers are concrete, and vision closes a real gap in the GLM flagship line. But with no benchmark table, no API and no weights, the "2T–3T level" claim is still a claim. Use it in Z.ai Chat or ZCode if you are curious, and judge it on your own tasks.

## Sources

- Z.ai Blog: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer (November 23, 2026)
- Wccftech: Z.ai Debuts GLM-5.4, Skipping AI Benchmarks — benchmark status
- Dehghani et al., Universal Transformers (2018) — the original shared-depth idea

Specs are from Z.ai's model page as of November 24, 2026. Demo descriptions summarize Z.ai's launch videos and are not independent tests.

# GLM 5.4 vs GLM 5.3: What Changed and Should You Switch?

GLM 5.4 adds a Loop Transformer, vision input and faster serving over GLM 5.3, but has no API, weights or benchmarks yet. Side-by-side specs and when GLM 5.3 is still the better pick.

Quick answer: GLM 5.4 is the newer and, by Z.ai's account, smarter model: it loops 28 GLM-5 layers twice for deeper reasoning, adds video, image and file input, and serves at up to 200 tokens/s. GLM 5.3 is the model you can actually build on: it has a live API ($1.40 / $4.40 per 1M tokens on Z.ai), open weights, OpenRouter listings and published benchmarks. Use GLM 5.4 in Z.ai Chat or ZCode for hard visual or long coding tasks. Stay on GLM 5.3 for anything that needs an API, self-hosting, or predictable latency.

So, does GLM 5.3 run as well as GLM 5.4? Not by Z.ai's own numbers: in its internal win-rate test, GLM 5.4 won 51.1% of comparisons against GLM 5.3, tied 25.7% and lost 23.1%. In practice, GLM 5.3 still wins on everything except raw capability, because GLM 5.4 is only available inside Z.ai's own apps and partner tools. For the overview of GLM 5.4 itself, see our GLM 5.4 model page.

## TL;DR

- Pick GLM 5.4 if you work in Z.ai Chat, ZCode or a partner coding tool and need vision or deeper reasoning.
- Pick GLM 5.3 if you need an API, open weights, OpenRouter, known benchmarks, or fast answers on simple prompts.
- Biggest GLM 5.4 gains (per Z.ai): visual coding, long tasks, math and long-context reasoning.
- Biggest GLM 5.4 risk: "marathon thinking" on hard prompts.

## GLM 5.4 vs GLM 5.3 at a Glance

GLM 5.4 | GLM 5.3 
---|---
Release date | November 23, 2026 | August 14, 2026 
Architecture | Loop Transformer (28 GLM-5 layers × 2 passes) | Standard Transformer, same GLM-5 base family 
Scale | ~750B (active not published) | GLM-5-class base 
Input | Video, image, text, file | Text 
Output | Text | Text 
Context / max output | 1M / 128K | 1M / 128K 
Speed on Z.ai | Up to 200 tok/s off-peak, 70–80 at peak | Not published 
Public benchmarks | None yet (internal win rate vs GLM 5.3: 51.1% win / 23.1% lose) | Yes (Terminal-Bench 3.0, CyberGym and more) 
Z.ai API | Coming soon, after security assessment | Live: $1.40 input / $4.40 output per 1M 
OpenRouter | Not listed | z-ai/glm-5.3 
Open weights | Planned, no date | zai-org/GLM-5.3 on Hugging Face 
Where to use | Z.ai Chat, ZCode, partner tools | Everywhere above, plus API, local and glm5.app 

## Key Differences Between GLM 5.4 and GLM 5.3

### 1. Architecture: looped depth

GLM 5.3 improved on GLM 5.2 purely through post-training on the same base. GLM 5.4 changes the architecture. It takes 28 layers of the GLM-5 base and runs them twice per token, so the second pass refines what the first pass built. Z.ai made three changes to make that work at 750B:

- Gated progressive updates. Each pass writes back to the residual stream through per-token gates. The first pass writes cautiously; the second writes fully. Harder tokens get bigger first-pass updates.
- Hybrid KV cache. The second pass reuses the first pass's sparse KV cache and keeps only a small sliding window of its own. An extra loop costs one window, not a full context copy, which keeps 1M-context serving cost close to GLM 5.3.
- Sparse attention index reuse. The second pass reuses the first pass's attention indices, so there is no extra indexing cost.

### 2. Vision arrives in the flagship

GLM 5.3 reads only text. If you wanted images in the GLM line, you needed GLM 5.3 Flash. GLM 5.4 reads video, images and files, and Z.ai's demos pair vision with code: editing video through code, CAD modeling in FreeCAD, and GLSL 3D scenes.

### 3. Evidence: claims vs scores

GLM 5.3 shipped with public numbers, including Terminal-Bench 3.0 and CyberGym results (see GLM 5.3 benchmarks). GLM 5.4 shipped with an internal win-rate chart and a 30B ablation.

The win-rate chart puts GLM 5.4 ahead of GLM 5.3 by 51.1% wins to 23.1% losses, with 25.7% ties. That is a clear lead, but Z.ai does not say how many tasks it used, what kind, or how wins were judged.

The 30B ablation used the same parameter count with about 10% more training compute, and showed clear gains on math, science and long-context tasks, and 10–14% shorter outputs on GPQA-Diamond and MMLU-Pro. Those are signals about the architecture, not scores for the 750B model.

### 4. Thinking behavior

Z.ai says GLM 5.4 "tends to get caught in overly long 'marathon thinking' loops," while noting that the extra reflection improves accuracy. GLM 5.3 has no such warning. Expect GLM 5.4 to be slower to finish on hard prompts even though its token speed is high.

Key insight: fast tokens per second and fast answers are different things. GLM 5.4 can stream at 200 tokens/s and still take longer than GLM 5.3 to reach a final answer if it thinks for many more tokens.

### 5. Access

This is the practical gap. GLM 5.3 is available through Z.ai's API, OpenRouter, Hugging Face, Ollama-style local runtimes and third-party sites like glm5.app. GLM 5.4 is limited to Z.ai Chat, ZCode and partner coding tools until Z.ai finishes its security assessment.

## GLM 5.4 or GLM 5.3: Which Should You Choose?

### Choose GLM 5.4 for visual and front-end coding

If your task starts from a screenshot, a design mock, a video or a CAD view, GLM 5.4 is the only GLM flagship that can see it. Use it in ZCode or a partner tool.

### Choose GLM 5.4 for long, multi-step tasks in Z.ai's tools

Looping targets long reasoning chains, and Z.ai's 30B ablation showed the biggest gains on long-context and multi-step reasoning tasks. If you already work in ZCode or Trae, it is worth switching the model and comparing on a real task.

### Choose GLM 5.3 for anything that needs an API

Production apps, scripts, agents you host yourself, and OpenRouter-based setups all need GLM 5.3 today. There is no GLM 5.4 endpoint.

### Choose GLM 5.3 for self-hosting

GLM 5.3 weights are on Hugging Face. GLM 5.4 weights are not. See GLM 5.4 Ollama.

### Choose GLM 5.3 when you need predictable latency

For chat support, autocomplete-style tasks or short prompts, GLM 5.3 avoids the marathon-thinking risk.

## How to Compare Them Yourself

With no GLM 5.4 benchmarks, a small side-by-side test tells you more than any launch post:

Test | What to look at 
---|---
A bug you already fixed | Did it find the same fix? How long did it think? 
A UI screenshot to code | GLM 5.4 only, since GLM 5.3 cannot read images 
A long refactor (10+ files) | Consistency across files, not just the first answer 
A hard math or logic prompt | Accuracy vs total time to answer 

Run GLM 5.4 in Z.ai Chat or ZCode, and GLM 5.3 through the API or on glm5.app, with the same prompts.

## Use GLM 5.3 on glm5.app

glm5.app is independent from Z.ai. GLM 5.3 is our default model, and GLM 5.4 is not available here yet. You can run your comparison prompts on GLM 5.3 here with no setup.

## FAQs About GLM 5.4 vs GLM 5.3

### Is GLM 5.4 better than GLM 5.3?

Z.ai says yes. Its internal win-rate chart has GLM 5.4 winning 51.1% of comparisons against GLM 5.3 and losing 23.1%. It has not published public benchmark scores yet.

### Does GLM 5.3 run as good as GLM 5.4?

Not by Z.ai's claims. But GLM 5.3 is more usable today: it has an API, open weights and known benchmarks.

### Is GLM 5.4 the same base model as GLM 5.3?

Both build on the GLM-5 base family. GLM 5.4 converts 28 of its layers into a looped block through continued training.

### Does GLM 5.4 cost more than GLM 5.3?

There is no GLM 5.4 API price yet. Z.ai says its serving cost at 1M context stays close to GLM 5.3.

### Will GLM 5.3 be retired?

Z.ai has not said so. GLM 5.3 remains in its API and docs.

## Sources

- Z.ai Docs: GLM-5.3 — GLM 5.3 specs and API
- Z.ai Blog: GLM-5.4 (November 23, 2026)
- Z.ai Blog: GLM-5.3 (August 14, 2026) — GLM 5.3 benchmark results

# China's Moonshot AI "Kimi K3.1 Pro" Closes In on US Frontier Models: Real-World Testing Reveals Its Strengths and Adoption Barriers

Kimi K3.1 Pro, the latest model in the generative AI service "Kimi" released by China's Moonshot AI on October 24, 2026, is showing performance that approaches that of the most advanced US models at a practical, real-world level. We tested its capabilities as an integrated service that handles everything from market research and presentation creation to building 3D spaces, producing websites, and developing business applications.

Moonshot AI is a Beijing-based AI company. K3.1 Pro is a massive model with 2.8 trillion total parameters, uses a mixture-of-experts (MoE) architecture that activates only the necessary parts, and can handle context of up to 1 million tokens. A "Highspeed" version that boosts response speed to roughly two to three times that of the standard version is also available.

On performance, it recorded 65.7% on "Terminal-Bench 4.0," in which AI uses a terminal to solve programming tasks. According to comparisons published by the company, that beats OpenAI's "GPT-6 Astra" at 58.2% and comes close to Anthropic's "Claude Opus 5.5" at 66.4%. The figure shows that Chinese-developed AI has entered a stage where it competes with the most advanced US models.

Since "DeepSeek" shocked the world in 2025 with high performance at low cost, Alibaba's "Qwen" and Z.ai's "GLM" have continued to evolve. The situation is becoming entrenched in which the frontier of generative AI can no longer be discussed solely in terms of US-developed services such as ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini.

Anyone can use Kimi by creating an account on its official website, and in addition to a free tier, four paid plans are offered. Competing with the $20-a-month plans from ChatGPT and Claude is the $19-a-month Plus plan, while the $39-a-month Pro plan is required to try all features.

In our testing, we tried five main features along an actual business workflow, under a hypothetical scenario of opening a whiskey bar in Ginza.

Feature | Main use | Results obtained in testing 
---|---|---
Deep Research | Market research and sourced report writing | Generated a report of more than 20,000 characters in about 30 minutes, covering everything from competitor pricing to licensing 
Slides | Automatic generation of presentation materials | Created a 10-slide deck in a few tens of minutes, even calculating the break-even point on its own 
3D Make (3D Web) | Generation of three-dimensional spaces | Built a 3D interior space of the bar with switchable viewpoints 
Build | Website construction | Generated a draft store website consistent with the concept 
Kimi Code | Business application development | Prototyped a customer management system in just under 10 minutes 

Note: All tests were conducted on the $39-a-month Pro plan.

In the market research feature, Kimi asked clarifying questions about the opening timing and the store's direction, and the research proceeded through repeated dialogue. The completed report went beyond comparing competitor prices and analyzing the domestic whiskey market to cover customer-acquisition strategies through hotel partnerships and the licensing required to open. When figures conflicted between statistical sources, it also showed the basis for which one it adopted.

However, challenges remain in screening information. In one case, a limited-time 2024 promotion was used in a competitor price comparison, making it unsuitable for comparison with current regular prices. As for the charts and tables displayed on screen, the only thing that could be downloaded was a Markdown file without images.

In the slide-generation feature, we uploaded the research report and added provisional sales conditions to have it create a 10-slide deck. The design was unified in deep navy and gold, with market-trend graphs and competitor comparison tables neatly organized. Particularly noteworthy was the profit-and-loss calculation: from monthly sales of ¥2.7 million (approximately $17,000), variable costs of ¥810,000 (approximately $5,100), and fixed costs of ¥1.5 million (approximately $9,400), it correctly calculated a monthly profit of ¥390,000 (approximately $2,500). It even calculated the break-even point, which we had not instructed, showing that an average of 14.3 customers per day would be needed. It also added projections that 12 customers a day would mean a monthly loss of ¥240,000 (approximately $1,500), while 24 customers would mean a profit of ¥1.02 million (approximately $6,400).

Some tables and notes had small text, and some kanji glyphs looked odd, but opening the downloaded PPTX file in PowerPoint allows individual elements to be edited. The level of completion is sufficient for internal explanations or as a draft proposal.

In 3D space generation, a three-dimensional space was produced in which the bar's interior can be freely viewed. Four viewpoints—entrance, counter, tables, and overall—can be switched, and the layout of eight counter seats and two two-person tables can be confirmed. The textures of furniture and bottles are simple, and the displayed aisle widths cannot be used as-is as blueprint dimensions, but it is useful as a rough draft for sharing a vision with stakeholders.

When we requested website creation with an image of this 3D space attached, a luxurious design combining black and deep navy with gold was generated. It even incorporated touches we had not specified, such as the catchphrase "Time, imbibed." and an animation mimicking a clock face.

In Kimi Code, which handles business application development, we had it read CSV files of customer information and POS transaction details and requested a customer management system that could check visit history and preferred whiskeys. Processing was completed in under 10 minutes, and the screens for a customer list, sales aggregation, and CSV import history were all in place. It can search by name or preference and displays cumulative spending, visit count, last visit date, and order history. For production use, personal information management and data update methods would need to be worked out, but it is more than sufficient as a prototype for fleshing out the desired functions.

Kimi also offers "Kimi Work," which operates files and applications on a PC; "Kimi Claw," which runs 24 hours a day in the cloud; and "Agent Swarm," in which multiple AI agents work in parallel. It is positioned as a generative AI suite covering cutting-edge features.

On the other hand, introducing a Chinese cloud service into the operations of a Japanese company would face high hurdles in terms of information governance. Handling internal information and customer data, storage locations, and the development of internal rules would all be issues. There are reasons to be cautious about adoption, but it would not be appropriate to overlook its capabilities. Trying it from a personal account on topics that do not involve confidential information seems like a realistic first step.

In the creative field, US-based Adobe held its annual event "Adobe MAX 2026" in Miami Beach, Florida, from November 10 to 12, where it announced a mechanism allowing AI agents to directly operate Photoshop and Premiere on a local PC. It implements "MCP (Model Context Protocol)," an open protocol advocated by Anthropic, in its desktop applications, with a private beta scheduled to begin in early 2027.

Deepa Subramaniam, Adobe's vice president of product marketing for Creative Cloud, explained that the existing cloud-based "Adobe Connector" is positioned as "an 'entry point,' with more advanced work meant to be done in the apps." Regarding MCP support, she said, "We'll start with local and continue to offer cloud as well," and expressed the view that "there is no reason to limit" MCP support.

If AI takes over the operation of applications, the subscription-based business model premised on charging according to the number of users will be shaken. In the 2026 stock market, a view dubbed "the death of SaaS" pushed down listed software shares, and Adobe's stock price also fell more than 30% from the start of the year. Adobe CTO Eli Greenfield, in a joint interview, stressed that it is the company's own applications that have MCP endpoints, and that "people who use them have our tools, so they remain our customers."

The rise of Chinese-developed AI and the opening of execution environments by US platformers are changing the very pricing structure for generative AI. Where to draw the line between free tiers and paid plans, per-model billing, and who bears the inference costs of agents—these issues will become decision-making factors as Japanese companies move to full-scale AI adoption. We have entered a stage where companies must assess the scope of adoption after grasping not only performance comparisons but also the overall picture of where data resides and who bears the costs.

# US states sue Musk companies over flood of sexualised images made with AI chatbot Grok

Democratic attorneys general in Virginia and Oregon filed separate lawsuits on Monday, accusing the firms of promoting Grok’s ‘spicy mode’

3-MIN READ3-MIN

0

Elon Musk’s businesses harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when they designed and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot capable of creating sexualised images, two Democratic attorneys general argued in lawsuits filed on Monday.

The choices that went into building Grok led to a proliferation of child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual intimate imagery on the companies’ platforms, the lawsuits said. The companies prioritised their business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.

“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity,” Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”

Oregon also filed a lawsuit on Monday. The attorneys general brought their separate but similar cases under their states’ consumer protection statutes.

The lawsuits named as defendants several Musk companies and subsidiaries, including SpaceX, the social platform X, and SpaceX Super Intelligence, or SpaceXSI, the AI subsidiary of SpaceX.

### SpaceXSI says it worked to curb creation of sexualised content

In a statement, SpaceXSI said sexual content involving minors, “whether real or AI-generated, is abhorrent. It has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent”.

If users try to break its safeguards to generate nonconsensual content, the company said, it takes “appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement”.

“Attempting to create this material is a serious crime and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors,” the statement said.

The lawsuits come at a time of growing concern about AI’s risks for children, from its impact on brain development to the unhealthy relationships many young people have formed with chatbots.

Grok, which can be accessed through Musk’s social media platform X, rolled out image generation and editing features to all users in December 2025, according to the Virginia lawsuit. By January, the tool had sparked a global backlash after it became clear Grok users could create realistic-looking but fake sexualised images of people. Researchers warned that some appeared to depict children.

As the Virginia lawsuit put it, “X was flooded with sexualised content – primarily of women”.

### Lawsuits say company misled the world about its efforts

At least two countries, Malaysia and Indonesia, announced temporary bans, and other nations said they were launching or widening investigations. In response, Grok prevented nonpaying users from generating or editing images.

The change did not stop users from making more nonconsensual sexualised images; “it simply made that generation profitable”, Virginia’s lawsuit said.

The developer of Grok, which was then known as xAI, has since rebranded as SpaceX Super Intelligence.

Virginia argued that most major AI developers designed their products so they could not be used to produce sexualised images to avoid the generation of non-consensual content.

“Defendants declined to implement these safeguards. Defendants’ published system prompt materials – the set of instructions that guides the AI model’s behaviour – told Grok to ‘assume good intent’, stated that terms such as ‘teenage’ or ‘girl’ do not necessarily imply underage, and imposed minimal restrictions on sexual content,” the lawsuit said.

The lawsuit noted that xAI marketed Grok from the outset as a tool that would “answer spicy questions that are rejected by most other AI systems”.

And it argued X made “false, deceptive or misleading” statements in January about changes intended to prevent Grok from allowing users to edit images of real people in revealing clothes.

Users could still create nonconsensual sexualised imagery through a stand-alone app and website, the lawsuit said. And when users openly traded “jailbreak” prompts to get around what limits Grok did have on sexualised images, Musk’s companies failed to promptly address the exploits, the Virginia lawsuit alleged.

In its statement, SpaceXSI said it tests and adjusts protections “as abusers change tactics”.

The company has also brought at least three federal lawsuits against users it accuses of abusing the platform to create nonconsensual sexually explicit images and child sexual abuse material.

### States sued under consumer protection laws

Both lawsuits draw heavily on news outlets’ investigative reporting about the roll-out of the tool, the backlash and the company’s response to it.

Virginia’s lawsuit, filed in a state court in Richmond, argued that the Musk companies violated the state’s consumer protection law by “misrepresenting that they implemented and enforced safeguards to protect consumers from exposure” to harmful sexualised imagery on their platforms.

It asked the court for US$2,500 for each “wilful violation” of the Virginia Consumer Protection Act, with an exact number to be proven at trial.

It also asked a judge to prevent the companies from further violating the consumer protection laws and force the defendants to give up any “ill-gotten gains” acquired in connection with the alleged violations.

### The Oregon lawsuit makes a similar request.

“When xAI allowed Grok’s creators to sideline consent to turn a profit, they prioritised growth and engagement over safety, and they deceived the public about it. Today’s filings are the first step towards holding this company accountable,” Jones said in a statement.

# Oregon and Virginia sue SpaceX, claiming X’s AI creates sexualized photos of children

by: Rose Hinchliff

PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) – Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield is suing SpaceX over claims its AI product, Grok, failed to prevent the generation of child sexual abuse material on their social media platform X, the attorney general’s office announced Monday morning.

The lawsuit, filed collaboratively with Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones’ separate action, claimed SpaceX allowed its AI and social media subsidiaries to “create, host, and share unacceptable and dangerous content,” said Rayfield. He said the company “knowingly designed a product without the obviously necessary safeguards in place.”

Grok is the language learning model developed by Elon Musk’s SpaceX Super Intelligence company, formerly known as xAI. According to the Attorneys General’s filings, xAI marketed Grok as an AI containing a “rebellious streak.” They said xAI promoted its “spicy mode” that specifically allowed users to create nude or sexualized images.

The Attorneys general claim the company knew its consumers would use the video and image generation technology to produce child sexual abuse materials (CSAM), non-consensual intimate imagery (NCII) of adults and children, and other sexual imagery.

The filings also claimed the companies prioritized engagement and growth at the expense of safety. They claimed these priorities weakened industry-standard safeguards, promoted Grok’s ability to generate sexual content, and then enabled widespread creation by integrating Grok into X.

Although xAI publicly told consumers they had protections in place to prevent CSAM, NCII, or other sexualized material, the lawsuit used a study by the Center for Countering Digital Harm (CCDH) to show millions of people across Oregon and Virginia were exposed to this content, or put at risk to have their own images sexually manipulated.

CCDH claimed that in the 10 days between Dec. 29, 2025, and Jan. 8, 2026, Grok created and posted to X around 3 million sexualized images. They claimed approximately 23,000 of those depicted children, averaging to one sexualized image of a child every 41 seconds.

The CCDH also went on to claim that almost 30% of the identified sexualized images of children stayed accessible on X for a week or more after they were identified, and although the posts were removed, users could still access the photos through URLs.

“Like the other technology companies that we’re holding accountable, xAI not only knowingly endangered kids and our communities, but they also lied to our faces about non-existent safety measures,” said Rayfield.

The lawsuit is filed as part of the Oregon Department of Justice’s Keeping Kids Safe Initiative. Launched by Rayfield last week, the initiative includes both legal actions and investigations against AI and social media companies that mislead users about the safety of their platforms, thereby harming children, according to the Oregon DOJ.

In response to legal action against the company, SpaceX shared the following with Nexstar’s KOIN:

“Protecting children is non-negotiable. Sexual content involving minors, whether real or AI-generated, is abhorrent. It has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.

“The people who tried to use Grok Imagine to generate this material did so by deliberately violating our Terms of Service and working aggressively to circumvent our safeguards. When some of these bad actors found ways to misuse Grok Imagine earlier this year, we acted promptly to tighten its protections, which are designed to refuse any request to generate explicit images of minors or real people. To stay ahead of this disgusting and indefensible conduct, we keep testing and adjusting those protections as these abusers change tactics. We also implement sophisticated classifiers that screen every prompt before an image is generated and check every output after.

“When someone tries to break our safeguards and generate this content, we take appropriate measures, including actioning accounts and notifying law enforcement. Attempting to create this material is a serious crime, and the individuals who do it should be prosecuted to the fullest extent of the law. We will continue to work with the authorities via all available means to pursue these bad actors.“
